issue.subject: [tools][infra][qem-bot] Wrong openQA job runs referenced in qem-bot `inc-approve`-runs size:S
issue.description:
## Observation
From https://suse.slack.com/archives/C02CANHLANP/p1765446174817959:

> @qa-tools I found a suspicious false negative in the bot. https://gitlab.suse.de/qa-maintenance/bot-ng/-/jobs/5724923 says:
> ```
> 2025-12-11 07:33:30 INFO     Found failed, not-ignored job https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065 for incident 1330
> 2025-12-11 07:33:30 INFO     git:1330 has at least one failed job in incident tests
> ```
> However, https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065 is green. Actually, looking at that specific build in openQA, there is nothing red.

For @nicksinger a local bot-run says https://openqa.suse.de/tests/20252253 is blocking (despite being a force-result soft-failed). Jose found that t20256065 is a clone of https://openqa.suse.de/tests/20252358 (which actually failed).
We should understand why the bot even mentiones these openQA jobs and fix it to use the most recent reference of a scenario.

Raising this with high prio as this might block some updates soon.

## Acceptance criteria
* **AC1:** qem-bot only references failed openQA jobs which are actually not ok, e.g. failed, incomplete, etc.
* **AC2:** qem-bot still clearly references blocking failures

## Suggestions
* The job is not very old, and the incident is correct in any case
* Start with https://github.com/openSUSE/qem-bot/blob/master/openqabot/approver.py#L288 where the log message "Found failed, not-ignored …" is sent
* Confirm how the job gets looked up with the wrong result
    * This could be the wrong result mapped to the mentioned job
* If you want to look up data in qem-dashboard follow https://gitlab.suse.de/qa-maintenance/bot-ng/#cleanup-of-unwanted-test-results, well, without the actual "delete" part :)
* For the original job

```
dashboard_db=# select * from openqa_jobs where job_id=20256065 limit 3;
     id     | update_settings | incident_settings |                                           name                                            |              j
ob_group              | status |  job_id  | group_id | distri |         flavor         |  arch   | version |     build     |            updated            | o
bsolete  
------------+-----------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------
----------------------+--------+----------+----------+--------+------------------------+---------+---------+---------------+-------------------------------+--
--------
 1352029984 |                 |           2309903 | sle-16.0-Online-Updates-Staging-aarch64-Build:1330:haproxy-qam_regression_firefox@aarch64 | Maintenance: S
LES 16.0 Core Staging | passed | 20256065 |      656 | sle    | Online-Updates-Staging | aarch64 | 16.0    | :1330:haproxy | 2025-12-16 14:16:47.520906+01 | f
(1 row)
```

journals.notes:
The job was marked as softfailed on 2025-12-11 08:29:57 +0000. The message was logged on 2025-12-11 07:33:30 which was before. So it makes sense that it didn't incorporate the label.

I'm not sure how the mentioned clone comes into play here.

So far this ticket doesn't seem valid to me.

mkittler wrote in #note-2:
> The job was marked as softfailed on 2025-12-11 08:29:57 +0000. The message was logged on 2025-12-11 07:33:30 which was before. So it makes sense that it didn't incorporate the label.
> 
> I'm not sure how the mentioned clone comes into play here.
> 
> So far this ticket doesn't seem valid to me.

Let's start from the beginning then. https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065 was mentioned in "Found failed, not-ignored job https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065 for incident 1330". https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065 is passed and has no comment. So it really looks like a non-altered, not-forced-result'd, passed job is seen by qem-bot as blocking. Taking a look into the audit log searching for "20256065" there is one entry https://openqa.suse.de/admin/auditlog?eventid=40467581 for the clone of the failed https://openqa.suse.de/t20252358 as https://openqa.suse.de/t20256065. How is the ticket not "valid" to you?

journals.notes:
livdywan wrote in #note-6:
> Related [report in Slack](https://suse.slack.com/archives/C02CANHLANP/p1766047567281909).

TLDR: We had the issue, that a job needed to be restarted with a different setting using the `openqa-clone-job` utility. However this clone is not part of the scheduled product anymore. Because it appears that the bot looks at the jobs of a scheduled product and not the most recent ones for a certain build, the bot will always look at the failed (outdated) job and not the cloned more recent one.

e.g. https://openqa.suse.de/tests/20331681 - this job is not part of the scheduled product, which the bot looks at.
Checking since this is nearing SLO for normal tickets - possible fix for the blocker was just merged, see #192904#note-13
